notes: UNITS: every table keeps its published units (see 'units'); Lapua drops and drifts are in MILLIMETRES (not cm), Federal/Hornady in inches/yards. Nothing in 'rows' was converted or interpolated; a 0 in a drop cell at the zero range is the published zero (blank in Federal's print). The top-level muzzleVelocityMps of Federal/Hornady loads IS a conversion from published fps (2720->829, 2710->826, 2600->792, 2900->884); the published value is in muzzleVelocityPublished and in each table's 'load'. Each table carries a 'load' object with ITS OWN inputs: several ids contain a second, different cartridge (Lapua) because the headline maker's table stops at 500 yd - never test the headline MV/BC against a table whose 'load' differs. REACH: 22lr 100 m; 223 500 yd only (no published 1000 table found for a 77 gr .223 load - null); 65cm Hornady 500 yd, Federal 500 yd, Lapua 136 gr 1000 m; 308 Federal 500 yd, Lapua 175 gr 1000 m; 300wm Federal 500 yd, Lapua 185 gr 1200 m; 338lm 1500 m; 308sub 300 m. SOURCES NOT REACHED: federalpremium.com and cci-ammunition.com sit behind a bot check and were not read; Federal data come from Federal's 2026 LE catalogue PDF and Federal spec sheets, so CCI Standard Velocity could not be documented (Lapua Center-X used instead). Federal's catalogue rows on p.14 carry no load numbers; they were matched to p.13 by row order within each product block (GM308M2 row cross-checked against a Federal web snippet). WIND: Lapua = 4 m/s (13 fps) full crosswind. Federal's LE catalogue does not print the wind speed; values are consistent with a 10 mph crosswind (Federal's usual convention) but that is my inference. Hornady publishes no drift. SIGHT HEIGHT: Lapua 40 mm, Federal 1.5 in, Hornady 1.5 in (inferred from -1.5 in at muzzle). ATMOSPHERE: Federal 59 F / 29.53 inHg / sea level (Army Standard Metro-like, not ICAO); Lapua and Hornady not stated. BC CAVEATS: Lapua says its rimfire BC (0.172) is computed by Quick Target Unlimited from V0 to V75 and applies to all its .22 LR bullets; Lapua centerfire tables are widely understood to be Doppler-radar based (QuickTarget/Lapua Ballistics, custom drag), so a single-G1 point-mass run will not match them exactly at long range - the 2011 Lapua brochure gives velocity-banded G1 values (338 Scenar GB488: 0.646/0.632/0.588/0.613/0.708; B416: 0.515 above 300 m/s, 0.413 below; 185 gr Scenar GB432: 0.485/0.472/0.439/0.457/0.657, G7 0.242). Sierra likewise publishes velocity-banded BCs for the MatchKings Federal loads; Federal's single numbers (0.372 / 0.505 / 0.533) are averages. Hornady quotes ELD-M BCs at Mach 2.25. DOUBTFUL: (1) Lapua .338 page lists MV 890 m/s in the spec block but 905 m/s in the table. (2) Lapua .300 WM 185 gr metric drift row looks inconsistent with its own imperial row (39 in at 600 yd vs 1229 mm at 600 m). (3) Lapua imperial tables contain misprints (.338: missing cells in the 300/600 yd rows; .300 WM energy 1947 ft-lb at 800 yd) - only metric tables were transcribed. (4) GM65CRD1 BC 0.535 and GM223M3 BC 0.372 are retailer-quoted. (5) GM223M3 MV: 2720 fps in catalogue vs 2730 +/- 25 in the 2020 spec sheet. (6) Rifle 'soldInFrance': null = could not verify for that chambering.

published.note: Published reference figures that are not trajectory tables. Quoted as printed; nothing computed.

litzSpinCoriolis.source: Bryan Litz, 'Gyroscopic (spin) Drift and Coriolis Effect', Applied Ballistics LLC (2021 reprint) - https://appliedballisticsllc.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Gyroscopic-Drift-and-Coriolis-Effect.pdf
litzSpinCoriolis.quotes: 'typically 8-9 inches at 1000 yards for small arms trajectories'; 'You can count on no more than 10 to 12 inches at 1000 yards'; 'about 2.5-3.0 inches to the right at 1000 yards' near 45 N; vertical '+2.5 to 3.0 inches (shooting east), or -2.5 to 3.0 inches when shooting west'; 'Firing due North or South results in zero vertical deflection'.

formulas.miller: Don Miller, 'A New Rule for Estimating Rifling Twist', Precision Shooting, March 2005: Sg = 30 m / (t^2 d^3 l (1 + l^2)), velocity factor (v/2800)^(1/3), air density factor.
formulas.litzSpinDrift: Bryan Litz, Applied Ballistics for Long Range Shooting: SD [in] = 1.25 (Sg + 1.2) tof^1.83.
formulas.litzAeroJump: Bryan Litz, Applied Ballistics for Long Range Shooting: vertical deflection [MOA per mph of crosswind] = 0.01 Sg - 0.0024 L + 0.032, L = bullet length in calibres.
formulas.g7Table: Standard G7 drag function (BRL), as tabulated in McCoy, Modern Exterior Ballistics, and in open-source solvers (py-ballisticcalc drag_tables.py TableG7, 84 points Mach 0 to 5).
